frontier.hypothesis: A DIFFERENTLY-SHAPED chassis (e.g. drop base_addr entirely and derive both p uses from arg0 via a computed expression that makes GCC track arg0's value through a callee-save naturally) - not a mutation of the s3 form but a rewrite of the C structure
frontier.mechanism: The residual is a copy-prop tie between $a0 (arg-reg with arg0) and $s4 (callee-save with base_addr). All s1-s3 structural probes and the s4 permuter mutations keep the same overall C shape (p and base_addr as parallel derivations from arg0). A structurally different shape - e.g. eliminating base_addr and letting GCC's own arg-live-across-call analysis materialize arg0 into $s4 - may sidestep the tiebreaker without codegen-steering constructs.
frontier.next_probe: s5 (structural/deep-dive): try (a) drop base_addr, use arg0 in both uses with an intervening operation on p that visibly extends arg0's live range across the loop; (b) inspect matched siblings for the arg0->$s4 pattern in cluster (AddTbpOfst_80047EE8 has register asm pins per s1 evidence, so its natural form is unknown - m2c-reconstruct target's original C shape to compare); (c) inspect target asm's staged prologue (`move s0,a0; move s4,s0; addu s0,s0,a1`) - the staged copy through $s0 first is a strong hint about original source structure (arg0 -> local1 -> local2 chain?)

frontier.hypothesis: The buf[8] unused array itself is the load-bearing lever - the WRITTEN-never-read carve-out could apply if the C source captures the efc_buki_draw_zanzou return into buf[k]
